<text:style bold="true">Colors</text:style>

<image:base64 col="0" width="21" wrap="none"></image:base64>

The Colors panel holds nine colours. Every colour is used as the primary colour (the
stroke: lines and outlines) or as the secondary one (the fill: the inside of the
figures). The two current colours are always shown in the bar at the bottom, one
over the other, with a button to swap them. The colours are applied to the selected
objects, or to the next ones if nothing is selected. The buttons of this panel are
always active.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">The nine colours</text:style>
A click gives the primary colour. A double click, Ctrl+click or the item
"Assign as secondary color" of the right button menu gives the secondary
       colour. The same menu has "Change color...", which replaces the colour of the
       button with another one of your choice (it is kept in the settings).

<image:base64 col="0" width="10" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Colors / Materials menu</text:style>
The title of the panel is a menu: it chooses whether the nine buttons are
colours or materials (see Materials).

The windows of the colours: a click on Stroke color or on Fill color in the
properties, or on the colours in the bar at the bottom, opens the window of the
colour, with the opacity too. If the stroke or the fill is a material, the window of
the material opens instead; each window has a button (Material... or Colour...) to
go to the other, so that a colour can be replaced by a material and the other way
round. The window of a stroke or fill colour has also a None box: with it checked
the colour is none (the outline is not drawn, or the inside is not filled), as with the
none box of the properties; choosing a colour in the window clears it.

The boxes that show a colour (the bar at the bottom, the Properties) also show how
transparent it is: a colour that is not opaque is drawn over a chequered ground, and the
more it is transparent, the more of the chequers show through.
